title: The Last Signal
description: You're a salvage operator answering a distress beacon in deep space. The beacon's registry matches your own ship — the one you're standing in.

n1.caption: The distress call repeats on a dead frequency. When the wreck resolves on your scope, the hull markings are yours: same ship, same scars.

choices.label: Scan it from a safe distance

n2a.caption: The airlock cycles without power. Inside, the corridors are your ship's — but older, dusted, and something has been living in them.

n2b.caption: The scan comes back: one life sign aboard the wreck. It's broadcasting your own heartbeat.

n3a.caption: On the bridge, the captain's chair faces away. It turns. It's you — fifty years older, mouthing two words: don't dock.

n3b.caption: The scratching leads to your own quarters. On the wall, written in frost: TURN AROUND. The airlock light behind you is green.

n3c.caption: Your engines flare — and the wreck flares with them, mirrored exactly. In the rear camera feed, its bridge light comes on. Someone is watching you leave.
